content:
ashley: Quick Q — can we show inline, contextual permission hints on the route editor when someone picks a model or routing policy?

sam: You mean like a little badge that says "Requires: route.write, model.use" next to the dropdown?

ashley: Exactly. Tiny help text that expands on hover. Also would be awesome if it showed the effective role(s) that would be impacted when you change routing.

tiffany: From product: +1. Most enterprise admins ask what will break when devs swap routing. If the console can say "This change restricts tenant-admins from using model X" that's useful.

ben: Security perspective: we need to be careful exposing too much about entitlement graphs. But a high-level hint is fine — like mapping to role templates instead of revealing bindings. e.g. show "affects: Tenant Admin, Service Account: billing-worker" (abstracted).

ashley: Right. Thinking low-risk: show the minimal permission set required by the route (list of permission names), and a list of role archetypes likely to be affected (not explicit principals).

sam: Implementation idea: compute "permission delta" for the proposed change on the backend (small endpoint) and return a compact summary. The UI just renders the strings. That keeps logic server-side and consistent with our auth model.

ashley: Prototype API sketch:
```json
POST /internal/perm-preview
{ "route_id": "r-123", "candidate_config": { "model": "redwood-llama-v2", "policy": "private-only" } }

// response
{ "perm_delta": ["route.invoke", "model.pull:restricted"], "role_archetypes": ["tenant-admin", "service-account"], "confidence": "high" }
```

sam: That looks fine. A couple notes: keep perf tight — this will be called while typing. Cache previews per route/config hash. Also rate-limit per user.

ben: Also add a flag in the response to indicate if the preview requires a deeper audit check (e.g., cross-tenant effects). If flagged, UI should show "requires audit" and link to docs.

tiffany: UX ask: make the hint non-blocking and collapsible. We want to avoid modal fear for small edits. Maybe a small chevron with "Permissions preview" that expands.

ashley: Agree. Also include a telemetry event when preview is expanded and when the user saves with a perm-impacting change. We need to track how often previews prevent risky saves.

sam: Telemetry event shape: 
PERM_PREVIEW_SHOWN { route_id, user_id, delta_count }
PERM_PREVIEW_SAVE { route_id, user_id, delta_count, changed: true }
We should not include any PII in the payload; user_id can be stable anonymized id.

ben: For audits we can attach the preview snapshot to the change record (hashed) so infra can recompute later without storing raw role bindings.

tiffany: One more: allow a preview toggle in org settings so enterprise accounts can set "preview required" for any route change to force review. That ties into rollout policies.

ashley: Sounds like next steps: 1) Sam to spec the internal API (perm-preview) with perf/caching constraints; 2) Ben to call out any additional security gating; 3) Tiffany to mock the small collapsible affordance and copy; 4) I’ll add telemetry events to the tracking backlog.

sam: I’ll drop a rough API spec in the PR and include cache TTL suggestions.

ben: I’ll review and list the audit flags.

infra-bot: deploy: staging updated for console-ui (build 2024.06.12-1123) :rocket:

ashley: Great — thanks. Putting this in the 2-week roadmap.

sam: FYI: also noticed some existing perm-preview endpoints in auth-svc that we can reuse. I’ll include notes in the PR.
